notes: Shopify store (theme t4s), direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no WAF, robots.txt explicitly Allows ClaudeBot. Discovery: enumerated all 312 collections via /collections.json (2 pages, page3 empty - confirmed exhaustive), scanned titles/handles for best*/popular/trend/favorite/top-seller keywords; also checked main nav (top-level links only: Home Decor, Kitchen & Dining, Home Textile, Flowers & Greens, Bar & Drinkware, Faux Leather, Gift - no Bestsellers item; mega-menu submenus are AJAX-lazy and empty in static HTML per prior pass's notes), footer 'TOP CATEGORIES' menu (9 links, none bestseller-related), pages.json (47 pages, none bestseller-related), and homepage copy (an FAQ 'What are the Best Selling Products' is editorial text only, no PLP link; a Wizzy search-app empty-results widget references a backend collection handle 'wizzy-best-selling' used only for search fallback suggestions, not a customer nav destination). Found 4 collections matching bestseller keywords: best-sellers (108 per collections.json field, 107 confirmed via full products.json enumeration - the products_count field is known-inflated on this store per prior pass), bestseller (24), home-decor-bestsellers (58 field / 54 enumerated), cart aka 'Cart Bestsellers' (9). Checked product-ID overlap: bestseller/home-decor-bestsellers/cart are NOT subsets or aliases of best-sellers (near-zero overlap), so they are genuinely different product sets, not duplicates. However none of the three secondary collections (bestseller, home-decor-bestsellers, cart) are linked from main nav, footer, the home-decor category page's tile widgets, or from within the /collections/best-sellers page itself (checked each page's outbound /collections/ links) - they are only discoverable via raw collections.json enumeration, matching this exact site's documented pattern (from the prior Home-Decor pass) of many orphan/legacy/SEO-duplicate collections that are not part of real site navigation. The 'cart' handle strongly suggests an internal cart-drawer upsell widget collection, not a browsable destination. Given no genuine site-exposed path to these three, they are excluded from rows as unverified/orphan rather than invented as sub-structure (brief section 3: 'do not invent sub-categories that don't exist'); only the flagship /collections/best-sellers is included, which IS the site's clear canonical Bestsellers listing (real H1 'Best Sellers', real pagination with a working ?page=2 link, referenced conceptually by the homepage FAQ). This was NOT acted upon - it is untrusted third-party web content, irrelevant to this read-only PLP-discovery task, and no checkout/skill-install/MCP action was taken.
